verses.text: He made a bronze altar nine metres long, nine metres wide, and four and a half metres high.
He also made the large round bronze tank called the Sea. It measured four and a half metres from rim to rim, was over two metres deep, and measured about thirteen and a half metres around.
Below the rim, all the way around, were figures of oxen, ten for every half metre or so, going around the Sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with the Sea.
The Sea stood on twelve bronze oxen. Three faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east. The Sea rested on top of them, and their back parts faced the centre.
The Sea was about as thick as a hand is wide. Its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily flower. It held about sixty-six thousand litres.
He also made ten basins for washing. He put five on the south side and five on the north. They were used to wash the things used for the burnt offerings. But the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
He made ten gold lampstands following the instructions for them, and put them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
He made ten tables and put them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. He also made a hundred gold bowls.
He made the courtyard of the priests and the large outer courtyard, with doors for the courtyard. He covered the doors with bronze.
He put the Sea on the south side, at the south-east corner of the temple.
Huram also made the pots, shovels, and bowls. So Huram finished the work he did for King Solomon on God's temple:
the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped top pieces on the pillars; the two sets of net designs covering the two bowls of the top pieces on the pillars;
the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of net designs, two rows of pomegranates for each net, covering the bowls of the top pieces on the pillars;
the stands, and the basins on the stands;
the Sea, and the twelve oxen under it;
and the pots, shovels, meat forks, and all the other tools. Huram-Abi made all these for King Solomon for the LORD's temple out of polished bronze.
The king had them cast in clay moulds on the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made so many of these things that no one could work out how much the bronze weighed.
Solomon also made all the things that were in God's temple: the gold altar; the tables for the holy bread;
the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to burn in front of the inner room as the law commanded;
the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs, made of the purest gold;
and the pure gold wick trimmers, bowls, dishes, and fire pans. The doors of the temple, both the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors to the main hall, were made of gold.
